What holds in the commit body (supabase/candidates/20261005_research_health_quick_order_intake.sql@121d0987):

- Read-only recovery runs first. The actor/key transaction lock and an exact replay follow, before any changeable gate (:364-370, :543-551).

- The two strict-reader calls are compared for equality. The reader returns text-only values, so the jsonb equality is byte-exact (:554, :649).

Compared with 25858ad, the reader bodies are unchanged except for comments, and the installer's compiled 5 s lock and 30 s statement timers are gone, which is an improvement.

findings.claim: Under SET search_path='' the session's pg_temp schema is searched first for type names (PostgreSQL 17 runtime-config-client), and jsonb, text and timestamptz are not grammar keywords. admin_detail is SECURITY DEFINER and granted to service_role. It declares and casts these types unqualified, and so does intake_valid, which admin_detail, replay (through admin_detail), the commit (:785) and the companion CHECK during the commit's INSERT (:811) all run as the owner. A service_role session with TEMP privilege could define a pg_temp domain named jsonb whose CHECK calls a pg_temp function. That function would then run as the superuser or BYPASSRLS owner. This is the same class doc 80 CS-2 rated P2 for currentness. The commit body itself is fully qualified, but the resealed qo_ddl (QO_INTAKE_TRANSACTION_V2) leaves the readers and helpers unqualified, while the correction map records qualification as authored.

findings.claim: Both TX03 cases (same key; same key with a changed payload) start two independent psql backends with Promise.all and nothing makes them overlap. When they don't overlap, the second call is answered by the pre-lock replay. The actor advisory lock and the post-lock second recovery and conflict branch are then never reached. If those were deleted, the control would still pass on any run without overlap.
findings.evidence: mjs:761-770@121d0987: no withSyntheticLock or awaitBlockedBy. intake.sql:364-369@121d0987 is the pre-lock replay; 543-544 is the actor lock; 545-551 is the post-lock replay and the conflict at :548. TX06-actor-admission (mjs:895-901) shows the commit waits on a holder's actor lock, but not the second-recovery outcome. Behaviour reasoned, NOT RUN.
findings.fix: Make the race deterministic. Stall commit A after it holds the actor lock, for example with a holder taking FOR UPDATE on A's row-11 session row. Start commit B, call awaitBlockedBy on A's backend pid, then release. Assert A has replayed:false and B has replayed:true with the same requestId and publicReference. For the changed-payload case, assert B gets 23505 'Quick Order key conflicts' with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT from the post-lock branch. For this control, use a synthetic lock_timeout large enough that the waits fit (IB-11).

findings.title: Two of the five try-lock controls doc 75 requires are absent

The verifier covers the exclusive holder, the abort window (holder rollback then same-key retry) and reentrancy. It lacks the queued-writer case and the shared-holders-granted case. A gate check that looked only at granted exclusive locks would pass every existing control.

LENS IC (adapter, handler, production): CORRECTIONS REQUIRED. Reasoned from source only; nothing was run.

findings.claim: QuickOrderRoutes schedules clear() at access-token expiry. clear() nulls current, increments accountEpoch, aborts in-flight requests and sets the boundary to null. QuickOrderPage then unmounts SessionForm (sessionKey null), and the held unresolved attempt and its in-memory key are lost. When TOKEN_REFRESHED later arrives for the same user, sameAccount is false, so a new key `quick-order:${epoch}:${userId}` and a fresh form are minted. A same-account customer whose token expires while confirmation is unresolved therefore loses the same-key recovery that doc 75's CC-10/R2-8 ruling relies on. This can happen after sleep, a hidden tab or offline time, which often accompanies a lost response. The customer can then resubmit under a new key and create a duplicate request. The transport already refuses expired tokens (App.tsx:121), so the timer-driven wipe adds no authority protection.
